title: Design Twitter's home timeline
question: How would you design the Twitter home timeline?

problem.statement: Design the home timeline for a service like Twitter: users post short tweets, follow other users, and see the newest tweets from the people they follow.
example: Post a tweet with text and optional photos
Home timeline: newest tweets from people you follow, and scroll for more
constraints: 200 million daily users, each opening the app ~10 times a day
The timeline loads in under 200 ms
A new tweet may take a few seconds to show up
problem.followUp: What happens when someone with 100 million followers tweets?

steps.caption: What the interviewer is really asking.

plain.asking: When you open the app, show *the newest tweets from everyone you follow*, instantly, even though thousands of different people wrote them.
points: *Must work:* post, follow, a newest-first timeline that scrolls.
*Must be fast:* opening the timeline, far more common than posting.
*Out of scope:* search, trends, ads, ranking by interest.

check.question: Why do the work when a tweet is posted, rather than when a timeline is opened?
options: Timelines are opened about 20× more often than tweets are posted
check.explain: Work done at post time is done *once*; work done at read time is repeated on every open. With 20 reads per post, pushing at write time wins.

check.question: Why not copy a star’s tweet into every follower’s list, like everyone else’s?
options: One tweet would mean 100 M copies and minutes of delay
check.explain: The cost of copying grows with the number of followers. For stars it explodes, so their tweets are *fetched when you read* instead.
